survey: A round analog clock with a thick orange rim, seen slightly from the left so the face is a mild ellipse and the rim's depth shows on the left side. It stands upright on the bottom of its rim on a green floor, right against the striped wall behind it, with a soft contact shadow under it. The white face has 12 hour marks in the right places and 4 minute dots in each gap between them. In the centre is a navy hub with a red cap. Three hands come from that hub: a short, thick hour hand pointing toward 10, a longer minute hand pointing toward 2 (about 10:10), and a thin red second hand pointing toward about 7. All the hands share the one pivot, lie flat over the face and stay inside the rim. The rim is a closed, even ring that fits the face. There are no extra parts, glows or gadgets. The clock has no foot or stand. It rests on its rounded edge, but it touches the floor and leans on the wall, the way a wall clock set down would. That is an acceptable simplification, not a floating or unsupported part.
